After a failure, the tree is recomputed; an eligible redundant port can become forwarding if a usable alternate path exists. [nf-stp-root-election.md]

On each segment, the port advertising the best root information becomes the **designated port**. With the same root ID, compare root path cost, then sender bridge ID and sender port ID. Root and designated ports forward data once the relevant state transitions have completed; a role alone does not imply immediate forwarding. [nf-stp-port-roles.md]

In this stable classic-STP example, an enabled redundant port that is neither root nor designated is **blocked**: it still listens to BPDUs but forwards no data. During convergence, even a root or designated port can temporarily be listening or learning. [nf-stp-port-roles.md]

The fix is **pipelining**: permit several frames to be outstanding (sent but not yet acknowledged). Use a loss-free fixed-frame model with no queueing, processing, ACK transmission or framing gaps. The formula defines the window size below. [nf-window-pipeline.md]
Consider the preceding stop-and-wait example: a 1 Gbit/s link, 30 ms propagation round trip, and 1500-byte frames. Each frame takes 12 microseconds to transmit: [nf-window-pipeline.md]

A layer-7 proxy can inspect application messages; a basic layer-2 bridge forwards by destination MAC and VLAN context, though the same device may provide other features. [osi-model]

Sustained offered traffic above a link’s service rate causes backlog or drops. High average utilisation can increase delay, but a utilisation number alone does not establish the queue state. [network-congestion]

Sending data again after loss, damage or an acknowledgement timeout. A successful retransmission can deliver previously missing useful data; goodput counts those bytes once, while all extra attempts consume capacity. [retransmission]
For a completed transfer with equal payload sizes, if 5% of attempts are extra retransmissions, unique delivered payload accounts for 95% of attempted payload. [retransmission]

A component coupling changing magnetic flux between windings to transfer electrical energy or signals. Separate, appropriately insulated windings can provide galvanic isolation; an autotransformer has a shared winding and does not. [transformer-electrical]
Ethernet magnetics can isolate the cable-side circuitry from equipment-side circuitry; the actual part and circuit determine isolation ratings. [transformer-electrical]
https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/tidu832b/tidu832b.pdf [transformer-electrical]
['electrical transformer', 'electrical transformers', 'isolation transformer'] [transformer-electrical]

A component storing energy in an electric field. In a series coupling path it passes changing signal components while blocking steady current after charging; actual frequency response depends on capacitance and the surrounding circuit. [capacitor]

Fiber Distributed Data Interface: a 100 Mbit/s token-passing fibre LAN standard using a dual-ring architecture and 4B/5B coding. Fast Ethernet also uses 4B/5B in particular PHYs; this entry makes no claim that all fibre networks use FDDI. [fddi]

A classic-STP port in the blocking state receives relevant BPDUs but does not forward user data or learn source addresses. In a stable simple topology this includes redundant enabled ports outside the root/designated forwarding set; role and state are distinct during convergence. [blocked-port]
With the stated 1500-byte frames, 1 Gbit/s link and 30 ms propagation round trip, stop-and-wait utilisation is about 0.04%, ignoring ACK time and other overhead. [stop-and-wait]
In the loss-free 1 Gbit/s model with 1500-byte frames and 30 ms propagation round trip, a 2501-frame window covers the full frame-plus-feedback cycle. [outstanding-frames]

The textbook alternating-bit stop-and-wait model uses a one-bit sequence number, with suitable ordering and packet-lifetime assumptions; arbitrary old duplicates cannot be handled by finite numbering alone. [sequence-number]

100BASE-TX is a 100 Mbit/s Fast Ethernet PHY over two twisted pairs, using 4B/5B and MLT-3 at 125 million symbol intervals per second. Fast Ethernet also includes other PHYs, so the family name is not synonymous with this one variant. [fast-ethernet]
Fast Ethernet is a PHY family, not an alias exclusively for 100BASE-TX. [fast-ethernet-family]

A Gigabit Ethernet coding/PHY family using 8b/10b at 1.25 gigabaud. It includes optical variants such as 1000BASE-SX and 1000BASE-LX and the short-reach copper 1000BASE-CX variant; not every member uses fibre. [1000base-x]

nf-model-responsibilities.rationale: No maths needed for layer responsibilities. The application-library scenario tests allocation of work; the retained bridge question isolates ordinary MAC lookup. The responsibility table and local/end-to-end distinctions supply the prerequisites.

questionsRewritten.nf-layered-models-q3: Replace model-layer recall with a responsibility scenario.

nf-encapsulation-demux.rationale: No formula needed: nesting and local Ethernet replacement explain demultiplexing and routing. The revised EtherType question supplies its mapping and the frame question asks why a new frame is needed; retained IPv4 forwarding options follow the explicit no-NAT/no-fragmentation assumptions.

questionsRewritten.nf-layered-models-q2: Provide the protocol mapping and test demultiplexing rather than hexadecimal recall.
questionsRewritten.nf-layered-models-q8: Replace counting routed frames with the hop-local framing mechanism.

nf-wire-efficiency.rationale: Remove repeated efficiency substitutions; the visible 100-byte/full-frame comparison and explicit frame/IP/wire boundaries suffice. Questions now diagnose omitted gap/preamble and displaced payload; neither needs a memorised byte count or equation.

questionsRewritten.nf-layered-models-q4: Replace layered-byte summation with frame-versus-wire accounting.
questionsRewritten.nf-layered-models-q7: Replace timestamp-option goodput calculation with the fixed-MTU trade-off.

nf-ethernet-header-parser.rationale: Retain the bounded Python parser because unpacking and its limits are the objective. No maths. The unchanged question tests what the 14-byte guard proves, with VLAN/FCS/full-frame omissions visible.

nf-layer-boundaries.rationale: No formulas needed for pseudo-header coverage, UDP deployability, MTU and cross-layer effects. The tunnel question now diagnoses the shared outer-IP budget. Retained keys explicitly distinguish ordinary routing, NAT, application proxies and loss mechanisms.

questionsRewritten.nf-layered-models-q10: Replace VXLAN MTU subtraction with identification of the correct encapsulation boundary.

nf-transmission-rate.rationale: Keep one optional size/rate relationship for later estimation; the prose states both effects and cancellation, and the road-lanes analogy remains optional. Questions test doubling size and rate together and bits versus bytes without requiring arithmetic.

questionsRewritten.nf-performance-q1: Replace routine packet-size/rate arithmetic with comparative transmission reasoning.
questionsRewritten.nf-performance-q4: Replace file-transfer calculation with diagnosis of bits, bytes and overhead.

nf-propagation-distance.rationale: Keep distance/speed as one reference relation, with fibre approximation, route and medium assumptions visible. Questions distinguish travel time from serialization, including a supplied radio/fibre model; removed substitution does not hide prerequisites.

questionsRewritten.nf-performance-q2: Replace distance/speed substitution with distinguishing transmission and propagation.
questionsRewritten.nf-performance-q3: Keep the existing prediction question; replace its unnecessary feedback equation.

nf-complete-hop-delay.rationale: Remove the four-term formula, repeated substitutions and nonessential delay calculator. Visible component definitions and a checked 5.26 ms example support diagnosis; the pipeline question tests concurrency across links, with store-and-forward and overhead assumptions explicit. The pipeline now uses a Markdown timing table with explicit zero-propagation/processing assumptions; the former explicit diagram was not compilable.

questionsRewritten.nf-performance-q9: Replace store-and-forward timing calculation with explanation of pipeline overlap.

nf-queue-utilisation.rationale: Keep only the M/M/1 wait relationship as reference. Poisson/exponential/infinite-buffer/stable-load assumptions and finite means at 50/80/90/99 percent remain visible. The revised question asks why spare service capacity clears bursts slowly, not for a queue calculation.

questionsRewritten.nf-performance-q7: Test nonlinear delay and model limitations without queue-formula substitution.

nf-flight-window.rationale: Keep BDP and the steady window/RTT bound as useful reference choices; payload-rate, feedback-delay and operating-system accounting assumptions are visible. All three questions predict larger flight allowance or diagnose an active receive-window limit.

questionsRewritten.nf-performance-q5: Replace BDP arithmetic with flight-size prediction.
questionsRewritten.nf-performance-q6: Replace receive-window throughput division with diagnosis of an active window constraint.
questionsRewritten.nf-performance-q10: Replace satellite RTT/window arithmetic with combined latency and flight-size implications.

nf-throughput-goodput.rationale: No equation required after retaining the checked 949/941 Mbit/s ideal ceilings and counting boundary. The revised question tests why retries consume a fixed saturated-link budget; it does not infer a universal TCP loss response.

nf-stp-recovery.rationale: No equations: timer values and guarded host-port assumptions are visible. Retain all three practical questions about delayed access, protocol transitions and superior-root protection; no universal recovery guarantee or all-traffic-through-root claim remains.

questionsRewritten.nf-error-control-q4: Replace hand CRC division with interpretation of the check and its stated convention.

questionsRewritten.nf-error-control-q3: Replace stop-and-wait utilisation arithmetic with its idle-time mechanism.

questionsRewritten.nf-error-control-q9: Replace maximum-window recall with diagnosing overlap and duplicate ambiguity.
questionsRewritten.nf-error-control-q10: Replace retransmission counting with why Go-Back-N and Selective Repeat differ after a gap.
